title: Exceptional fibres over a smooth target are rational trees
statement: Let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-weil-field], so for each $x\in K^\times$ either $x$ or $x^{-1}$ belongs to $V$. Suppose $K$ is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] and the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Set $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $W\to T$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], of pure relative dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with smooth generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $f:Z\to W$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], an isomorphism on the generic fibre and between schematically dense open subschemes. Schematically dense means that $\mathcal O\to j_*\mathcal O$ is injective for the open inclusion $j$. Suppose $Z\to T$ is flat and finitely presented of pure relative dimension one and is semistable: the singularities of every geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are ordinary nodes, with completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over an algebraically closed residue field $\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $x\in W$ be a point at which $W\to T$ is smooth, and suppose $Z_x=Z\times_W\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ has positive dimension. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] of $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $s$ be the composite geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to W\to T$. The reduced geometric fibre $B=(Z\times_W\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme] is a nonempty connected nodal curve with finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components], each isomorphic to the projective line $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ [def-sc-p1-standard]. Its dual graph, with one vertex per component and one edge per nodal intersection, is a tree (connected with no cycles). The set of intersection points of $B$ with the closure of $Z_s\setminus B$ in $Z_s$ has cardinality at most two. Neither $W$ nor $Z$ is required to be separated or proper over $T$; no stability or marking assumption is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.2, printed pp. 30--31, and Appendix B: exceptional projective-line-tree structure of a positive-dimensional modification fibre over a smooth point; unmarked case. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-modification-proper-completion] to $f$ and $x$. Its source-reducedness hypothesis follows directly from flatness: apply [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] on every affine open of $Z$ with the invertible module $\mathcal O$. Multiplication by each nonzero element of $V$ is injective, so its coordinate ring injects into its generic localization; the generic fibre is smooth and hence reduced, so a nilpotent in the chart is zero. All geometric fibres of $Z/T$ are nodal by hypothesis, so the required neighbourhood is semistable. We obtain $R=V_{\mathfrak p}$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, proper flat finitely presented integral curves $\bar Z,\bar W$ with geometrically reduced fibres, and a proper modification $\bar f:\bar Z\to\bar W$. The target is normal, their generic fibres are geometrically integral and identified, and the original map is unchanged over an open $U$ containing $x$. Over the given $\Omega$, put $D=\bar Z_\Omega$, $C=\bar W_\Omega$ and let $y\in C$ be the single induced point. It is smooth, the map is an isomorphism off $y$, and $(\bar f_\Omega^{-1}(y))_{\mathrm{red}}$ is the original $B$, with an open ambient neighbourhood unchanged. This reduction asserts properness only for the auxiliary completions.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.2, local-to-proper reduction using Lemma 4.4.1; flatness check for reducedness expanded.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proper-normal-geometric-connectedness] first to $\bar f$. Its target $\bar W$ is normal integral and its source is integral, with its generic point mapping to that of $\bar W$. Its generic fibre over the function field of $\bar W$ is a single point with that field, because $\bar f$ is an isomorphism on dense opens. Thus its generic global functions are that field. The conclusion makes $\bar f$ geometrically connected, so $B$ is connected and nonempty; reduction does not change its space. Apply the same node to $\bar Z\to S$. The localizations of a valuation ring are integrally closed: if $a\notin R$ is integral over $R$, then $a^{-1}\in R$, and its monic equation, multiplied by $a^{-(n-1)}$, expresses $a$ as an element of $R$, a contradiction. Thus $S$ is normal integral. The integral source dominates $S$, and its proper geometrically integral generic fibre has global functions $K$ by [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety](2). Consequently $D$ is connected. Its surjective image $C$ is connected as well.

source.place: Tag 0AY8, label lemma-geometrically-connected-fibres-towards-normal; Temkin Lemma 4.4.2, connectedness paragraph.

proof.text: The curves $D,C$ and the geometric fibre of the original $Z/T$ are of finite type over $\Omega$, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The reduced closed subset $B$ has dimension one by the hypothesis and the completion identification. It is a union of finitely many whole curve components together with possibly finitely many isolated points: a closed proper subset of an irreducible Noetherian curve has dimension zero. Points not on its one-dimensional components would be isolated connected components of $B$, which connectedness excludes. Thus $B$ is pure of dimension one. Near it the ambient curve is nodal. At a node its reduced subcurve consists of one branch (smooth) or both branches (nodal), as seen from $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$; elsewhere it is smooth. Therefore $B$ is nodal. Properness of $D$ follows from [lem-pc-proper-base-change], and its closed subcurve $B$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a),(c). Let $B_1,\ldots,B_v$ be its components, $e$ its internal nodes (including self-nodes), and $r$ its boundary points in $D$. These sets are finite. Since $C$ is a curve and $D\setminus B\cong C\setminus\{y\}$, the complement is nonempty. Connectedness of $D$ therefore gives $r\geq1$: if the two unions of components did not meet, they would partition $D$ into two nonempty closed and open subsets.

source.place: Appendix B, boundary of a reduced subcurve; local nodal branch and connectedness arguments expanded.

proof.text: For each of $p:\bar Z\to S$ and $q:\bar W\to S$, apply [lem-pc-rf-perfect-base-change] to its structure sheaf. It is of finite presentation as a module over itself and flat over $S$, and both structure morphisms are proper finitely presented. Thus $Rp_*\mathcal O_{\bar Z}$ and $Rq_*\mathcal O_{\bar W}$ are perfect and compute structure-sheaf cohomology after arbitrary base change. By [def-pc-perfect-complex], around the closed point of the local scheme $S$ each is represented by a bounded complex of finite projective $R$-modules; an open containing that closed point is all of $S$. By [lem-trf-projective-over-local-free] the terms are free, and finite generation makes their ranks finite. For any field over $S$, tensoring such a complex gives terms of those same ranks. The identities $\dim H^i=\dim P^i-\operatorname{rank}d^i-\operatorname{rank}d^{i-1}$ telescope, so the Euler characteristic of its cohomology is the alternating sum of the integer ranks of its terms, independently of the field. Hence $\chi(D)=\chi(\bar Z_\eta)$ and $\chi(C)=\chi(\bar W_\eta)$, even for the given algebraically closed residue-field extension $\Omega$. Their identified generic fibres give $\chi(D)=\chi(C)$. This uses integer dimensions, with no reduction modulo the residue characteristic.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-nodal-contraction-euler-defect] to $D\to C$, the smooth point $y$, and $B$. Properness, reducedness, the one-dimensional connected fibre, the isomorphism off it and the nodal neighbourhood have all been checked. Its normalizations $\widetilde B_i$ are smooth proper connected curves; put $g_i=\dim_\Omega H^1(\widetilde B_i,\mathcal O)\geq0$. The formula and Step 4 give $0=v-e-r-\sum_i g_i$, or equivalently
$$0=(r-1)+(e-v+1)+\sum_i g_i.$$

source.place: Appendix B, Lemma B.1 and Corollary B.2 numerical calculation, smooth-point case.

proof.text: The dual multigraph of $B$ is connected, since a partition of its vertices without an edge across it would partition the connected curve $B$ into disjoint unions of components. Starting at one vertex, repeatedly adjoin an edge to a vertex not yet reached; connectedness supplies such an edge until all $v$ vertices are reached. The selected $v-1$ edges form a spanning tree, so $e-v+1\geq0$. Step 3 gives $r-1\geq0$, and all $g_i$ are nonnegative integers. The equality in Step 5 forces $r=1$, $e=v-1$, and every $g_i=0$. Every edge is therefore in that spanning tree. In particular there are no cycles, multiple-edge cycles, or self-loops.

source.place: Appendix B, Corollary B.2; elementary finite connected multigraph and nonnegative-integer calculation.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-genus-zero-smooth-proper-line], each $\widetilde B_i$ is $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$. A self-node on $B_i$ would be a self-loop of the dual graph, which Step 6 excludes. Apply the branch statements of [lem-trf-nodal-normalization-adjunction] to $B_i$ in the ORIGINAL geometric fibre $Z_s$, which is nodal everywhere by hypothesis; the completion need be nodal only near $B$. This node says that the only singularities of the reduced component are self-nodes, and that its normalization is an isomorphism on its smooth locus. There are no self-nodes, so the normalization is an isomorphism everywhere, and $B_i\cong\mathbf P^1_\Omega$.

source.place: Tag 0C6U, proposition-projective-line; nodal branch description as in Temkin Appendix B.

proof.text: At a point of $B$, membership in the boundary is detected on the preserved open neighbourhood: at a node it means that one branch is a component of $B$ and the other is not; a smooth point of the ambient curve is not a boundary point. The identifications over $U$ identify these branches in $D$ with those in the original $Z_s$. Thus the original set $B\cap\overline{Z_s\setminus B}$ has exactly $r=1$ point, in particular at most two. Together with Steps 2, 3, 6 and 7 this gives all the asserted nonemptiness, connectedness, nodality, finiteness, projective-line components and tree clauses.
